deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is not about the interval addition of the previous page. It is a draft of the foundations of the real numbers via cuts, essentially the material of §5 of Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen (1872). A real number α is the cut (A1, A2) of the rationals; β is the cut (B1, B2). By the convention used, every a1 in A1 satisfies a1 ≤ α and every a2 in A2 satisfies a2 ≥ α.

(1) Fragment, top left: 'Wäre nun β > α ...'. The definition of order being used is: β > α if there is a rational in B1 that is not in A1. So if β > α, there is a rational b'1 ∈ B1 with b'1 ∉ A1. Since (A1, A2) partitions Q, b'1 ∈ A2; the interlinear insertion names it b'1 = a'2. Because b'1 ∈ B1, we get β ≥ b'1 = a'2 ≥ α. The contradiction this is meant to produce lies on a page we do not have, so the purpose is not certain. My reading: it is part of showing that some β cannot exceed α (one half of an identity or ordering argument).

(2) Left column: proof that a cut (𝔄1, 𝔄2) of the real domain R is produced by the real number α. Here α is the number defined by the induced rational cut: A1 = 𝔄1 ∩ Q and A2 = 𝔄2 ∩ Q. Let β be any real number with β ≠ α. There is a rational a strictly between α and β; this fact is proved in (3).
- Case β < α: then β < a < α (the struck letter b was corrected to a).
- Since a < α and a is rational, a ∈ A1, hence a ∈ 𝔄1.
- Since β < a, also β ∈ 𝔄1. Reason: every element of 𝔄2 is greater than every element of 𝔄1, so β ∈ 𝔄2 would give β > a, a contradiction.
- The symmetric case β > α ⇒ β ∈ 𝔄2 is not written (implicit, mine).
- Conclusion, implicit and mine: every number < α lies in 𝔄1 and every number > α lies in 𝔄2. So α produces the cut, and it is the only number that does (Dedekind's continuity theorem for R).

(3) Right column: lemma that between two distinct reals there are infinitely many rationals. If α > β, then A1 contains (insertion) 'unendlich viele verschiedene' numbers lying in B2. A struck attempt at notation appears in between. Among these there are also infinitely many different from both α and β. Each such c satisfies c < α, 'weil sie der Klasse' A1 angehört; the text breaks off here. The intended completion is: and c > β because c ∈ B2. Hence β < c < α, with infinitely many such rational c. This supplies the rational a used in (2).
errors: Order of drafting: paragraph (2) uses the existence of a rational between α and β before paragraph (3) proves it. This is an expository ordering issue, not a logical error.
In (2) only the case β < α is treated; the case β > α (β ∈ 𝔄2) is omitted, presumably as symmetric.
Fragment (1) is incomplete: the contradiction or conclusion drawn from β ≥ a'2 is not on this page.

Paragraph (3) breaks off mid-sentence ('weil sie der Klasse'). The claim of infinitely many rationals of A1 lying in B2 is asserted, not proved here; it follows from A1 having no greatest element when α is not rational, or by a density argument.

results.what: Every cut (𝔄1, 𝔄2) of the real numbers is produced by exactly one real number α (completeness of R constructed by cuts)
results.modern_name: Dedekind completeness of the reals / continuity theorem
results.usually_credited_to: Richard Dedekind, Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen (1872), §5

results.what: Between two distinct real numbers (cuts) there are infinitely many rationals
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind 1872 (§5) in the cut construction; classical

results.what: Order of cuts: β > α iff B1 contains a rational not in A1 (equivalently, one lying in A2)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of arguments published nearly verbatim in Dedekind's 1872 Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen, §5: the order of cuts, density of rationals, and continuity of R. It is well known as his.

checkable.asserts: Instance of density: a rational lies strictly between two distinct reals (beta=7/5 < a < alpha=3/2 analog; here sqrt(2) lies between rationals, and e.g. 141/100 lies between 7/5 and sqrt(2))
A rational c with beta < c < alpha for beta=7/5, alpha=sqrt(2)
A further distinct rational between the same reals, illustrating 'infinitely many'

transcription_corrections: Line 'Ist β < α, so ist β < [-b-] a < α': the image shows a struck letter before a, consistent with the transcription.

Right column, first line: the insertion above 'mindestens' reads 'unendlich viele'. 'verschiedene' is written above a struck word; the whole phrase reads 'mindestens unendlich viele verschiedene in B2 enthaltene Zahlen'.
Right column, struck line: an abandoned notation attempt resembling '𝔄 𝔄 A2 ... A1 ... B2', not 𝔠/C; illegible, but clearly deleted.
In (3) the final words 'weil sie der Klasse' break off at the page end; the expected continuation 'A1 angehört' is not on the page.
